title: Hierarchical aggregation layer for inference KPIs (Prometheus + OTLP)
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Inference KPIs (per-request latency, token counts, error rates) produce extremely high cardinality across tenant, model, route, and quantization profile labels. Our current ingest pipeline either drops labels (losing observability) or ingests everything (unbounded cost and Prometheus remote_write blowups).

Goal: Build a hierarchical aggregation layer that: (1) accepts OTLP metrics and translates them into tiered Prometheus-compatible rollups, (2) produces tenant-aware rollups at multiple resolutions (route/model-level, tenant-level, global), and (3) preserves tail behavior via exemplar pointers and targeted raw-forwarding for flagged tenants.

Design summary:
- Sidecar-compatible aggregator runs near the ingest front-end; stateless workers perform time-windowed rollups with adaptive window sizing based on QPS and variance.
- Two-stage aggregation: local worker produces fine-grained short-term rollups (10s windows) + exemplars; central rollup scheduler compacts into medium (1m) and long (10m) series for remote_write.
- Histogram alignment: convert OTLP explicit histograms and summary metrics into Prometheus-compatible buckets using dynamic bucket selection derived from observed p50/p95/p99.
- Tenant-aware sampling: maintain full raw-forward for a configurable fraction of tenants (for debugging/regressions) and deterministic hash-based sampling for the remainder to control cardinality.
- Metadata tags: preserve route/model/version as label when tenant-level cardinality budget allows; otherwise promote those labels into a "high-cardinality" annotation stored in a sparse side-channel (S3/elastic) with exemplar pointers.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to close ticket):
1) Aggregator prototype reduces aggregated Prometheus series by >= 65% on the pilot tenant set while preserving p50/p95/p99 within ±5% of raw ingestion for 90% of routes.
2) End-to-end CPU cost for ingest path increases < 15% compared to baseline; network egress to remote_write decreases by >= 50% on pilot.
3) Exemplars correctly link to request traces (via OTLP trace IDs) for at least 95% of p99 events sampled.
4) Feature flags exist to toggle per-tenant raw-forwarding and to adjust sampling budget without restarts.
5) Integration tests and a canary run are documented; dashboard widgets show aggregated vs raw delta and exemplar link success rate.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Aggregation reduces observability fidelity; balancing the sample budget against cost savings is a product decision. We will provide a per-tenant SLA knob.
- Complexity: introduces additional components near ingest; prioritize a stateless first pass to ease operational burden.
- Long-tail debugging needs: we rely on exemplars + targeted raw-forwarding; investigate automatic escalation when regression monitors fire.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement prototype sidecar and central rollup with feature-flagged path (internal-only).
2) Pilot on two high-volume tenants for 4 weeks; run synthetic traffic generating known tail events to validate exemplar linkage.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% of tenants with monitoring on cost and delta metrics; adjust sampling budgets.
4) GA with Admin console controls for sampling/rollup budgets and tenant exemptions.
